questions.question: How many events are there in decathlon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Decathlon **is a combined event in athletics **consisting of ten track and field events.**
 
• The events in decathlon are **100 meters**, **400 meters**,**1500 meters**, **110 meters** of **hurdles**,** ****long jump**, **shot put**, **high jump**, **discus throw**, **pole vault**, and** javelin throw.**
 
• The pentathlon events that took place at the **ancient Greek Olympics** gave rise to the decathlon.
 
• Pentathlons comprised five events: sprint, discus throw, javelin throw, long jump, and wrestling battle.
 
• This **competition was first held at Olympia in 708 BC**, and for many centuries it was incredibly popular.
 
• The **modern decathlon** made its **debut **in the **Olympic athletics **schedule during the **Stockholm Games in 1912.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Male competitors** normally engage in the **decathlon**, while **female competitors** usually compete in the **heptathlon**.
 
• The **events are spread across two days**, and the athlete with the highest total score at the end of the competition is declared the winner.
 
• The** winner of the decathlon** has traditionally been crowned the** "World's Greatest Athlete."**
 
• With a total score of 9,126 points in the 2018** Décastar in France**, Frenchman **Kevin Mayer holds the current official decathlon world record.**

questions.question: Articles 25 to 28 of the Indian Constitution deal with __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rights to freedom of religion.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Articles 25 to 28** of the Indian Constitution are part of the Fundamental Rights which gives **Rights to freedom of religion.**

 
 
• **Article 25 **guarantees the** freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess**, practice, and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• **Article 26** grants every religious denomination the** right to manage its own affairs in matters of religion**, subject to public order, morality, and health.
 
• **Article 27 **prohibits the state from compelling any person to pay taxes for the promotion or maintenance of any particular religion** **or religious denomination.
 
• **Article 28** prohibits the imparting of religious instruction in any educational institution wholly maintained out of state funds.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rights to constitutional remedies**: **Articles 32 to 35 **of the Indian Constitution deal with the right to constitutional remedies.

 
 
• These articles** empower citizens to petition the Supreme Court or High Courts for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights** and other legal rights.
 
 
 
• **Cultural and educational rights**: **Articles 29 and 30** of the Indian Constitution deal with cultural and educational rights.
 
 
• **Article 29** provides** protection for the interests of minorities** by prohibiting discrimination on the grounds of religion, race, caste, language, or any of them.
 
• **Article 30 grants minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions** of their choice.
 
 
 
• **Right against exploitation**: **Articles 23 and 24** of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
• **Article 23** **prohibits trafficking in human beings** and **forced labour.** 
 
• **Article 24 prohibits** the **employment of children below the age of 14** in factories, mines, and other hazardous occupations.

questions.question: Per capita income represents the average __________ earned by a person in that country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Income**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Per capita income** is a measure of the** average income earned** by an individual in a particular country.
 
• It is** calculated by dividing the total income of a country by its total population.**
 
• It is a useful indicator of a country's economic well-being and can be used to compare the standard of living across different countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Income**: This refers to the **money earned** by an individual or business from various sources such as wages, salaries, investments, and profits. 

 
 
• It is an important measure of economic activity and is used to **gauge the financial health** of individuals, businesses, and countries.
 
 
 
• **Loan**: This refers to the **amount of money borrowed** by an individual or business from a lender.
 
 
• It can be used for various purposes such as buying a house, starting a business, or financing education. Loans **come with interest rates and repayment terms** that need to be fulfilled by the borrower.
 
 
 
• **Capital**: This refers to the** assets owned** by a company or individual such as property, equipment, and investments.
 
 
• It is an important measure of wealth and is used to **determine the financial strength** of a company or individual.
 
 
 
• **Liability**: This refers to the **debts owed** by a company or individual such as loans, mortgages, and credit card balances.
 
 
• It is an important measure of financial obligations and is used to **determine the financial risk** associated with a company or individual.

questions.question: Which of the following festivals is not celebrated in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nuakhai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nuakhai **is a **harvest festival **celebrated mainly in **western Odisha** and some parts of **Chhattisgarh **and **Jharkhand **and is celebrated with great enthusiasm and fervor.
 
• It marks the **beginning of the harvest season** and is a time of thanksgiving and celebration.
 
• The day following the Ganesh Chaturthi celebration, it is **celebrated on panchami tithi**, or the fifth day, of the lunar fortnight in the month of **Bhadrapada or Bhadraba (August–September).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Taj Mahotsav** is a festival celebrated in **Agra, Uttar Pradesh**, to **showcase the rich cultural heritage** of the state.

 
 
• It is a **10-day festival **that showcases the art, craft, and culture of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It is held **annually in February-March** and attracts a large number of tourists from all over the world.
 
 
 
• **Ganga Festival** is celebrated in **Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh,** to celebrate the holy river Ganges and its significance in Hindu mythology.
 
 
• It is celebrated in the** month of November **and is a major attraction for tourists who come to witness the grand celebrations and take a dip in the holy river Ganges.
 
 
 
• **Buddha Festival** is celebrated in **Sarnath, Uttar Pradesh, **to **commemorate the birth, enlightenment, and death of Lord Buddha.**
 
 
• It is celebrated in** Sarnath, which is a famous pilgrimage site for Buddhists.**
 
• It is held **annually in December** and is a major event for Buddhists from all over the world.

questions.question: Electrolysis of water is an example of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Decomposition reaction.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Electrolysis of water** is a **decomposition reaction** because it breaks down water into its constituent elements, hydrogen and oxygen.
 
• Reaction: **2H₂O + electricity → 2H₂ + O₂**
 
• **Electrolysis **is the **process of using an electric current to drive a non-spontaneous chemical reaction.**
 
• It is commonly used for the production of metals, such as aluminum and copper.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bidisplacement reaction** is also known as the **double displacement reaction.**

 
 
• It involves two reactants exchanging their ions to form two new products.
 
• For example, potassium nitrate reacts with aluminium chloride and forms aluminium nitrate and potassium chloride. 
 
• Reaction: **KNO₃ + AlCl₃ ↔️ Al(NO₃)₃ + KCl**
 
 
 
• **Displacement reaction** is also known as the **single replacement reaction.**
 
 
• It involves a more reactive element displacing a less reactive element from its compound.
 
• The reaction of potassium with magnesium chloride is an example of a single displacement reaction.
 
• Reaction: **2K + MgCl₂ → 2KCl + Mg**
 
 
 
• **Combination reaction** is also known as the **synthesis reaction**.
 
 
• It involves two or more reactants combining to form a single product.
 
• For example, when we** burn magnesium** ribbon (or magnesium), it gives a **gray-black ash of magnesium oxide.**
 
• Reaction: **Mg + O₂ → MgO**

questions.question: Which of the following liquids has the highest surface tension?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Surface tension** is the measure of the **force required to stretch or break the surface of a liquid.**

 
 
• The** SI unit** of Surface Tension is Newton per Meter or **N/m.**
 
• It is important to note that the surface tension of a liquid is **dependent on factors** such as **temperature**, **pressure**, and **impurities**.
 
 
 
• **Water (H₂O) **has the **highest surface tension among the given options** due to its** strong hydrogen bonding** between the water molecules.
 
 
• This results in a** strong cohesive force between the molecules**, making it difficult to break the surface.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH)** is a volatile, colorless liquid that has a slight odor.

 
 
• It burns with a blue flame that is smokeless and sometimes invisible in normal light.
 
 
 
• **Ethane (C₂H₆)** is **a gas** at room temperature and **does not have a surface tension value.**
 
 
• At standard temperature and pressure, ethane is a colorless, odorless gas. ​
 
 
 
• **Methanol (CH₃OH)**, also known as **wood alcohol**, is considered an alternative fuel.
 
 
• It is often **used as a low surface tension testing substance** in calibration and/or testing of new apparatuses or methods to measure surface tension.

questions.question: What is India's share in the world's water resources?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **India's share in the world's water resources** is** 0.04 or 4%**.

 
 
• It accounts for **18% of the world's population.**
 
• It accounts for about **2.45 per cent of world’s

 surface area.**
 
• The **total water available from

 precipitation** in the country in a year is **about

 4,000 cubic km.**
 
 
 
• India is one of the most water-stressed countries in the world, with a rapidly growing population and increasing demand for water.
 
• The major rivers in India are the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Indus, which are all shared with neighboring countries like China, Nepal, and Pakistan, leading to water sharing disputes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There is an ample supply of water worldwide, making it a cyclical resource.
 
 
• **Water covers roughly 71% of the earth's surface** but **fresh water** makes up only **approximately 3 percent of all water.**
 
 
 
• Climate change is exacerbating water scarcity in India, with irregular monsoons and increasing temperatures leading to droughts and reduced availability of water.
 
• India is working towards increasing water conservation efforts and improving water management to ensure sustainable use of its limited water resources.
 
• There are **four major sources of surface water**: **rivers**, **lakes**, **ponds**, and **tanks**.
 
• The groundwater utilisation is very high in the states of Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: In cricket, when a ball bowled as per rules passes the batsman without touching the bat or batsman and runs are scored on that ball, then those runs are considered as ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bye**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bye**: A run is scored when the batsman does not touch the ball with either his bat or body. First recorded in the 1770s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**A** glossary of cricket terms**:

 
 

 **Terms**
 **Explanation**
 
 

 Leg-Before Wicket (LBW)
 It's a way to get the batter out. In other words, the hitter is out if the umpire determines that the ball struck any portion of the batter's body—typically the leg—prior to striking the bat or missing the bat and would have struck the stumps.
 
 

 Maiden
 An over where no runs that are attributable to the bowler are scored (byes or leg-byes may be scored in this over, though, as these don't count against the bowler).
 
 

 Wide Ball
 A delivery that pitches too far away from the batsman and so proves impossible to score off. The umpire will single this by stretching his arms out horizontally; an extra will be added to the total and the ball will be bowled again.
 
 

 Bouncer
 A short-pitched ball which passes the batsman at chest or head height
 
 

 Chinaman
 A ball bowled by a left-arm slow bowler that turns into the right-hand batsman, in effect a left-arm legspinner. Named after Puss Achong.
 
 

 Mankad
 A term popular mainly in indoor cricket - but also fairly popular in Australia for outdoor cricket. Mankad is when the bowler brings his arm around and, instead of releasing the ball, runs out the non-striker by whipping off the bails. This type of dismissal is rare - and usually a warning is given to the batsman beforehand. Named after Vinod Mankad, who twice dismissed Australian Bill Brown this way.
 
 

 Doosra
 A Hindi/Urdu word which means "second" or "other", the doosra is the offspinner's version of the googly, delivered out of the back of the hand and turning away from the right-hand batsman.

questions.question: Unemployment is measured in India on the methods prescribed by the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__National Sample Survey Organisation.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Unemployment **is **measured in India** on the methods prescribed **by **the **National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO)**.

 
 
• According to the **International Labour Organization (ILO)**, **unemployment **is defined as** not having a job but is available for work and actively looking for one.**
 
• The **unemployment rate** is measured as the **ratio of the unemployed to the labour force.**
 
• The total number of employed and unemployed people is known as the** labor force.**
 
 
• People who are neither employed nor jobless, such as students and people who perform unpaid household labor, are seen as not being in the labor force.
 
 
 
 
 
• The **NSSO **is the nodal agency responsible for **conducting surveys and collecting data on various socio-economic aspects** of the country, including employment and unemployment.
 
 
• It was **set up in 1950** to conduct periodic surveys on employment and unemployment, which are used to estimate the unemployment rate in the country.
 
• In **2019**, the Central Statistical Office (**CSO**) and the National Sample Survey Office (**NSSO**) **combined **to **become **the **National Statistical Office (NSO)** under **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MOSPI).**
 
 
 
• Apart from NSSO, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) also publishes data on employment and unemployment, but it is primarily focused on the banking and financial sector.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **National Employment Department** under **Ministry of Labour & Employment** is responsible for formulating policies and schemes for employment generation and skill development in the country.
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is India’s central bank.
 
 
• In compliance with the terms of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934,** it was **founded **on **April 1, 1935** in **Calcutta**.
 
 
• It was permanently** moved to Mumbai in 1937.**
 
 
 
• Though originally privately owned, since **nationalisation in 1949**, the Reserve Bank is fully owned by the Government of India.
 
• It regulates the** issue of Bank notes** and **keeping of reserves** with a view to securing** monetary stability in India **and generally to operate the currency and credit system of the country to its advantage.
 
• It also monitors the monetary policies through its **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC).**
 
 
 
• The **National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE)** was **founded **in **1992 **with the main goal of** increasing market transparency in India's equity markets.**
 
 
• It was **recognised **as a stock exchange** by SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) in1993** and started its **operations in 1994.**
 
• Its **headquarters is in Mumbai.** It is a market facilitator for trades in wholesale debt, stocks, and derivatives.
 
• In **1994**, it **became the first exchange in India to provide modern, completely automated electronic trading.**

questions.question: Sitara Devi was famous for which of the following classical dances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sitara Devi** was known for **Kathak**, which is a classical dance form of North India that involves storytelling, intricate footwork, and graceful movements of hands and arms.
 
• Sitara Devi was a world-famous Kathak dancer, singer, and actress.
 
 
• She was **born **to her **father Sukhdev Maharaj** and her **mother was Matsya Kumari** on **8 November 1920 in Kolkata.**
 
• She is known as **"Queen of Kathak"**
 
• She was also referred to as the** "Empress of Dancing" or "Nritya Samrajni" by Rabindranath Tagore.**
 
• She was the recipient of several awards and accolades like the **Sangeet Natak Academy award (1969)**, **Padma Shri(1973)**, **Kalidas Samman 1995**, and **Nritya Nipuna**.
 
• She **died **at the age of 94 on** November 25, 2014.**
 
 
 
• **Kathak **is a **classical dance** form of **North India basically Uttar Pradesh.**
 
 
• It is a storytelling dance that involves intricate footwork, spins, and graceful movements of the hands and arms.
 
• The **themes **of Kathak are **often romantic or devotional in nature.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kathakali **is a classical dance form of **Kerala**.

 
 
• It is a highly stylized and **ritualistic dance drama** that combines elements of ballet, opera, masque, and pantomime.
 
• The performers wear **elaborate costumes and makeup** to **depict characters from Indian mythology.**
 
 
 
• **Bharatnatyam **is a classical dance form of **Tamil Nadu.**
 
 
• It is a highly expressive dance that involves intricate footwork, hand gestures, and facial expressions.
 
• The **themes **of Bharatnatyam are **often devotional in nature,** and the dance is often performed in temples.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri **is a classical dance form of **Manipur**.
 
 
• It is a graceful and fluid dance that involves delicate hand gestures, flowing movements, and intricate footwork.
 
• The **themes **of Manipuri are** often mythological or devotional** in nature.

questions.question: In India, stagnation in agriculture during colonial rule was permanently eliminated by ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Green Revolution.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 Green Revolution:

__
 
• The Green Revolution was a major initiative that aimed to increase the production and quality of food crops, especially wheat and rice, in India.
 
• In India, stagnation in agriculture during colonial rule was permanently eliminated by Green Revolution.
 
• It** **introduced new technologies, such as **high-yielding varieties of seeds, fertilizers, pesticides, irrigation**, and **mechanization.**
 
• MS Swaminathan is considered the father of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• Norman Borlaug is known as the 'Father of Green Revolution' in the world.
 
• the Government of India launched the Green Revolution in 1965 under the Third Five-Year Plan(1961-66).
 
• The Green Revolution within India led to an increase in agricultural production, especially in Haryana, Punjab, and Uttar Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial licensing:**

 
 
• **In 1970**, the government implemented the new industrial licensing regime based on the **Dutt Committee's **suggestion.
 
• **Its goals were as follows:**
 
 
• to **outlaw trade restrictions and monopolies** **(except by government)**
 
• to** avoid the consolidation of economic power** in a small number of hands
 
• To be able to manage monopolies
 
• To **safeguard the interests of customers**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Old crop technology**:
 
 
• It refers to** traditional farming methods,** which were prevalent during colonial rule.
 
• These methods were inefficient and could not keep up with the growing population's demands.
 
 
 
• **Loan facility**:
 
 
• It is a facility in which** borrowers receive a fixed amount of money up front in return for certain lending conditions.**
 
• With either a fixed or variable interest rate, borrowers agree to repay their lenders a predetermined amount over a predetermined timetable.
 
• It is a **general term and does not specifically relate to agriculture**. While access to credit is important for farmers, it is not a comprehensive solution to the challenges faced by the agricultural sector.

questions.question: Which of the following rulers established the Shunga dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pushpmitra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pushyamitra** ** established the Shunga dynasty in India** after **overthrowing **the **Mauryan ruler Brihadratha ****in 185 or 186 BC.**

 
 
• His **capital was at Pataliputra.**
 
• He successfully repelled the assaults of **Demetrius **and **Menander**, two Greek monarchs.
 
• Additionally, he **stopped the Kalinga king Kharavela's attack** and **conquered Vidarbha.**
 
• The **Stupas at Sanchi and Barhut** were **restored **during his rule. He constructed the Sanchi stone entrance with sculptures.
 
• He **patronised** the **Sanskrit grammarian Patanjali** under whom he performed **Vedic sacrifices** such as **Ashvamedha**, **Rajasuya** and **Vajapeya**.
 
 
 
• The** Shunga dynasty **ruled from** 185 BCE to 73 BCE** and was known for its** patronage of Buddhism and revival of Hinduism.**
 
 
• It emerged in the post-Mauryan era and had ten emperors who **ruled for roughly 112 years.**
 
• They controlled **North-central and Eastern India** as well as parts of the northwest (now Pakistan).
 
• Their **capital city was Pataliputra.**
 
• **Protecting India against the Huna invasion** was one of the Sunga dynasty's greatest accomplishments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agnimitra **was the **son of**** **Pushyamitra who ascended to the throne in his place.

 
 
• He **ruled **from roughly **149 BC to 141 BC**.
 
• Vidarbha had already seceded from the empire by this point.
 
• The** protagonist of Kalidasa's poem Malavikagnimitram is Agnimitra.**
 
• He was succeeded as king by his son Vasumitra.
 
 
 
• The **fourth emperor of the Shunga Empire** in North India was **Vasumitra**.
 
 
• He was the brother or half-brother of Vasujyeshtha, the stepson of Queen Mālavikā, King Agnimitra's third wife, and the son of Agnimitra through his queen Dharini.
 
 
 
• The identities of Vasumitra's successors remain unclear. Various names, including Andhraka, Pulindaka, **Vajramitra**, and Ghosha, appear in multiple accounts.
 
• **Devabhuti **was the **final known Sunga ruler.** The previous one was Bhagabhadra.
 
• In approximately 73 BC, **Devabhuti was assassinated by his own clergyman, Vasudeva Kanva. **The **Kanva dynasty **was created in Magadha and lasted from** 73 to 28 BC.**

questions.question: That part of agricultural produce which is sold by farmers in the market is called ________ surplus.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Market**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **"marketable surplus"** describes the **difference between a farmer's entire output and his own consumption of that output.****​​**

 
 
• **Market surplus** is the **part of agricultural produce which is sold by farmers in the market.**
 
• It is an important aspect of agricultural economics as it helps to determine the supply and demand of agricultural produce in the market.
 
• It can also influence the prices of agricultural produce in the market
 
 
 
• Agricultural produce refers to the crops and livestock produced by farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__.**

 
• **Revised surplus**: This refers to the **difference between the expected yield of a crop and the actual yield**.

 
 
• It is calculated by subtracting the expected yield from the actual yield.
 
 
 
• **Balanced surplus**: This refers to **a situation where the supply of agricultural produce in the market is equal to the demand** for it.
 
• **Imported surplus**: This refers to the **surplus produce that is imported from other countries** to meet the demand for agricultural produce in the local market.

• **The Nagpur INC Session of December 1920** saw the **acceptance and endorsement** of the non-cooperation programme without any resistance.
 
• The campaign was characterized by the boycott of foreign products, government services and legal practice, legislative bodies, courts, and government-run institutions and colleges.
